name: Shorts 330 / 360 / C-23 Sherpa
variants: C-23A / C-23B Sherpa (military cargo variant of the 330)
summary: Boxy, slab-sided twin turboprop nicknamed 'the flying shoebox', used as a commuter, a freighter and by the US Army and National Guard as the C-23 Sherpa.

wings: High, straight wing braced by a strut on each side
Wing sits atop a deep, rectangular fuselage
engines: Two PT6A turboprops in nacelles on top of the wing
fuselage: Extremely boxy, slab-sided rectangular fuselage with a flat belly and a rounded nose
Landing gear retracts into large blister sponsons on the lower sides
Sherpa has a rear cargo ramp
tail: 330 / C-23A/B: twin fins and rudders like the Skyvan
360 / C-23B+: a single tall swept fin and rudder

tellTales: Boxy, slab-sided fuselage with a flat belly
High wing with a strut on each side and engines on top of the wing
Landing gear bulges (sponsons) on the lower fuselage sides

confusedWith.howToTell: The Skyvan has fixed wheels in its sponsons, a blunter nose and a shorter fuselage; the 330/360 has retracting gear and a longer fuselage.
The C-212 has an unbraced high wing with engines on the leading edge; the Shorts has wing struts and engines perched on top of the wing.
The Dornier 228 has a long pointed nose and no wing struts; the Shorts is a squared box with wing struts and a blunt nose.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
